title: GCD power-of-two conjecture for the coefficients of $c_m(c_1)$
statement:
For $m\geqslant 2$, write the polynomial $c_m(c_1)$ as

$$
c_m(c_1)=\sum_{j=0}^{r_m}p_{m,j}c_1^j,
$$

where $r_m$ is defined by the paper's equation for the structure of $c_m(c_1)$. Let the greatest common divisor of its coefficients be

$$
\operatorname{g.c.d.}\,c_m(c_1):=\operatorname{g.c.d.}\{p_{m,0},p_{m,1},\ldots,p_{m,r_m}\}.
$$

Here $z_m\geqslant1$ is an integer sequence.

**GCD power-of-two conjecture.** For every $m\geqslant2$,

$$
\operatorname{g.c.d.}\,c_m(c_1)=2^{z_m}.
$$

The paper notes that divisibility by $2$ for all $m\geqslant2$ follows from the recurrence relation, while the asserted exact power-of-two form is suggested by computer calculations.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.17278

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2023).
source_name: A. V. Kitaev and A. Vartanian, “One-Parameter Meromorphic Solution of the Degenerate Third Painlevé Equation with Formal Monodromy Parameter a=i/2 Vanishing at the Origin”, arXiv:2305.17278 (2023).
